transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-11 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Avery Cole (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Cosmos Head of ML), Marcus Huang (Platform Eng), Priya Sen (CTO)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on milestones across access/setup, benchmark plan, midpoint review, and exec readout. Agreed success criteria: p99 latency <= 250ms for short prompts, throughput of 250 reqs/min for batch scenario, and no PII leakage with KMS-backed encryption. Security docs and access checklist to be shared; mid-point review scheduled ~3 weeks in; exec readout at end of sprint.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria & KPIs
- Workload sizing and synthetic vs production benchmarks
- Access model: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) and initial network setup
- Timeline, gates (kickoff, access, mid-point, exec readout), and owners
- Risks: data residency, SSO, audit logs, throughput test scaffolding

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery: okay everyone thanks for joining, this is the kickoff for the Cosmos POC, um the goal today is to align milestones and sign off on the bench metrics and what access we need, Samir will do the perf and bench plan details.
[00:17] Priya: thanks avery, quick context: we want to evaluate latency and cost tradeoffs for a customer support reranking pipeline and a short form generation microservice, both are bursty midday, approx 250 qps peak for rerank but averaged over steady state maybe 40 qps, ok sorry those numbers vary depending on the channel.
[00:35] Samir: cool, that's helpful, when you say rerank is that per user request or batched?
[00:39] Priya: mostly per user, but we also run nightly batch re-score for 10M rows, that's lower priority for the POC though.
[00:48] Lena: and we have strict p99 SLOs, anything over 300ms spikes users complain, so we're hoping Redwood can hit p99 under 250 at our typical payload size ~120 tokens.
[01:05] Avery: copy that, so let's put success criteria as p99 < 250ms for short prompts, average cost per 1k tokens under your internal target — we'll capture that later — and we need behavioral parity for quality, we'll use a seeded prompt set to measure regressions.
[01:24] Marcus: security question — we need SOC2 compliance evidence, and KMS integration for keys. We also prefer VPC peering or private deployment for the initial run. Is that possible?
[01:38] Samir: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC peering and we can also do a dedicated pool. there is an ops setup step: you'll need a service account and specific firewall rules; also for SAML SSO we need metadata from your IdP.
[01:54] Priya: can you send the SSO checklist? we have an internal security review next week.
[01:58] Avery: absolutely, I'll send the SSO and network checklist after this call.
[02:05] Samir: on the benchmarks, propose two tracks: 1) latency-first (small batch, low-latency routing) for the online endpoint; 2) throughput-first (bigger batching, amortized cost) for nightly ops. We'll run both with your sample inputs.
[02:23] Marcus: for throughput track we care about token throughput and memory/kv cache behavior — we've seen weird evictions in other runtimes, so we'd like to surface KV cache hit rates during bench.
[02:34] Samir: good call, we'll instrument KV cache hit/miss, per-token CPU/GPU utilization, and tail latency histograms. some transcriptions note: "K-V cache" spelled a few ways in older notes.
[02:48] Lena: what about model variants — can we test a quantized variant to save cost?
[02:52] Avery: yes, Redwood has quantization profiles. We'll propose a baseline model and a 4-bit quant candidate; Samir will outline perf/quality tradeoffs.
[03:05] Priya: timeline wise, how long to stand up access and run the initial bench?
[03:09] Samir: access checklist + service account setup typically 3 business days after we get network details and creds; initial bench runs can be 2-3 days after access. so from kickoff we'd expect a mid-point review at ~3 weeks.
[03:23] Avery: proposed gates: kickoff (today), access & smoke tests (by 2026-02-15), midpoint readout (week of 2026-03-02), exec readout (week of 2026-03-30). does that alignment work?
[03:38] Priya: yes that feels right. we may need an earlier tech deep dive for our infra folks.
[03:43] Marcus: I can be on that; i want to validate egress rules and TLS cert handling, also audit log format for compliance.
[03:54] Samir: we'll also capture request/response sample logs with redaction rules; we won't store PII, and at rest encryption via KMS is supported. noted risk: if their compliance team wants on-prem air gap we'll need sales to escalate a private deployment timeline.
[04:12] Lena: for success criteria we also want quality gates: no more than 2% regression on our rerank NDCG metric versus current model and no hallucination regression on a held-out eval.
[04:23] Avery: perfect, we'll build a small eval harness and run that daily during the POC.
[04:29] Priya: can you share sample benchmark spreadsheet? we want to see the fields you'll collect.
[04:33] Avery: yes, Samir will post a spreadsheet with columns for p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU util, cost per 1k tokens, KV cache hit rate, and quality metrics.
[04:42] Samir: i will also include test scripts for load generation and a seed prompt set, plus a runner for large-batch nightly testing.
[04:50] Marcus: minor nit, we need to measure cold-starts because some of our workflows are spiky, is warmup included?
[04:56] Samir: yes we'll include cold-start tests and a steady-state window. Also note that quantized variants can have different cold-start characteristics.
[05:07] Priya: any blockers from Redwood side?
[05:10] Avery: not from product; if compliance wants extra paperwork we'll loop in our security team. commercial: once we validate the benchmarks we can move to a committed dedicated pool if needed.
[05:21] Lena: ok next steps then are clear. we'll provide workload logs and a contact for IdP metadata, redwood sends the access checklist, samir posts bench template. mid-point in ~3 weeks.
[05:35] Avery: i'll follow up with calendar invites and the checklist. thanks everyone.
[05:40] Priya: thanks, bye.

Call wrap / Notes:
- Tone: pragmatic, security-aware, engineering-first.
- Main risks: audit paperwork timelines, VPC peering lead time, quantized quality regressions.
- Decision points: if latency/quality tradeoffs don't meet gates, evaluate dedicated pool or smaller model revision.
- References mentioned: benchmark spreadsheet link (placeholder: https://redwood.internal/bench/cosmos-2026), security pack v2 (link noted), sample prompt set (attached by Samir after call).
